hypothesis: 365-day recency is more useful when player-specific I2 history is deep enough to support adaptive talent estimates; 730-day recency is more useful as a variance stabilizer when player history is sparse.
comparison: exact Phase31B 365-day predictions versus current 730-day combined-lean predictions
support_data_rule: For each game, count only I2 terminal PAs strictly before the game date. Same-date PAs are excluded to avoid doubleheader/postgame leakage.

pregame_support_dimensions.pitcher_min: minimum prior I2 PA count across the two scheduled starters
pregame_support_dimensions.batter_median: median prior I2 PA count across the 18 projected/confirmed lineup hitters
pregame_support_dimensions.batter_q25: 25th percentile prior I2 PA count across the 18 lineup hitters

diagnostics.continuous: Within each development season, regress per-game delta log loss (365 minus 730; negative favors 365) on log1p(support) for each precommitted support dimension.
diagnostics.stratified: Within each season and support dimension, form support quartiles from pregame support only and compare pooled 365-minus-730 log loss by quartile.
diagnostics.uncertainty: Cluster pooled game-level loss differences by calendar date.

proceed_rule: Advance to an adaptive-recency model only if at least one support dimension shows (a) a negative support interaction slope in at least 3 of 4 development seasons, (b) pooled 365 performance is better in the highest-support quartile, and (c) the lowest-support quartile is worse or materially less favorable than the highest-support quartile. Otherwise retain universal 730 and stop the adaptive-recency branch.
exclusions: threshold tuning before the diagnostic passes
note: This phase tests whether support-dependent recency is empirically justified; it does not choose a threshold or promote a model.
